selected_topic.title: Apollo 12’s lightning strike and the SCE switch
selected_topic.angle: During Apollo 12’s launch, lightning disrupted spacecraft telemetry and the guidance platform. Flight controller John Aaron recognized the pattern from an earlier Apollo pad test and suggested switching the SCE to auxiliary, restoring the data stream.
selected_topic.viewer_value: The viewer can understand how prior familiarity with an unusual system behavior helped an engineer identify a real-time spacecraft problem and offer a specific recovery action.

sources.claim: The contemporary Apollo 12 technical air-to-ground transcript records the commander reporting loss of the platform and multiple caution lights, then Houston saying ‘Try SCE to auxiliary’ at 1:36; after the crew switches, the mission is cleared to continue staging.
sources.location: Apollo 12 Technical Air-to-Ground Voice Transcription, Tape 1/1, page 1, timestamps 00:01:02–00:02:06; transcript introduction identifies the text as verbatim air-to-ground communications.

sources.claim: Former Apollo 12 flight director Gerald Griffin recalled that Aaron had seen similar data loss during an earlier Apollo pad test; switching to AUX restored data by bringing another signal-conditioning line into the loop.
sources.location: Johnson Space Center Oral History Project transcript, Gerald D. Griffin interview, 12 March 1999, lines 329–348 (printed pages 12-11 to 12-12); participant recollection, not a contemporaneous transcript.

sources.claim: Apollo 12 was struck by lightning at 36.5 and 52 seconds; the latter caused an electrical disturbance. John Aaron suggested the SCE AUX setting, described there as Signal Conditioning Electronics, and the crew returned data.
sources.location: NASA Science page, ‘Lightning Strikes Twice’, main text and image caption; searched 2026-11-12.

sources.claim: NASA history describes the SCE as Signal Conditioning Equipment; switching from Normal to Auxiliary restored the spacecraft systems, and Apollo 12 continued into orbit and proceeded to the Moon.
sources.location: NASA history article, paragraphs on the 36- and 52-second incidents and launch recovery; searched 2026-11-12.

audience: General English-speaking Shorts audience; assume no prior knowledge of Apollo spacecraft systems.
uncertainty: NASA sources vary in expanding SCE: the NASA Science page says ‘Signal Conditioning Electronics’; the NASA history article and Gerald Griffin oral history use ‘Signal Conditioning Equipment’. Narration therefore calls it a signal-conditioning system without asserting either expansion. Contemporary Apollo transcript confirms the exact instruction ‘Try SCE to auxiliary’; Griffin’s later recollection supports the earlier pad-test connection but does not date it to exactly one year earlier. Script avoids the exact one-year claim.
topic_overlap: Run context reports no prior topic history. A visible archive scan shows nearby Paper Detour topics including the Great Emu War, Berlin Wall, Great Stink, Hansa marketplace operation, and scientific/engineering topics; no Apollo 12 episode was found in the listed archive files.
rejected_angles: A generic ‘lightning nearly destroyed Apollo 12’ framing was rejected because sources confirm a serious telemetry disturbance and recovery, not destruction or a near-loss of the mission.

thumbnail_promise.target_viewer: General viewers drawn to a clear, high-stakes spaceflight problem.
thumbnail_promise.verified_object_or_fact: A Saturn V struck twice by lightning and a rarely used SCE AUX switch suggested by John Aaron.
thumbnail_promise.promise: After lightning scrambles Apollo 12’s data, one obscure switch brings the signal back.
thumbnail_promise.open_question: What did Mission Control tell the crew to switch?
thumbnail_promise.payoff: The narration names SCE to AUX and explains that the auxiliary setting restored useful readings.
thumbnail_promise.visual_promise_payoff: Paper rocket under a lightning bolt with a small AUX switch in foreground; reveal the switch and recovering telemetry as the payoff.

assisted_review.review_scope: Independent factual check of the prior script revision 4f61f8d86f603c683d0551d8e828937765d9682864301b6fd3b999553fad2fe2; reviewer had already read the research notes, so this is not blind first-listener review.
assisted_review.finding: NASA Science expansion of SCE was misattributed; prior test and exact quote lacked support among the original saved sources.
assisted_review.resolution: Corrected the NASA Science attribution, avoided expanding SCE in narration, added the official verbatim Apollo 12 air-to-ground transcript for the exact instruction, and added Gerald Griffin’s NASA oral-history recollection for the earlier pad test. Removed the unsupported exact one-year timing.
assisted_review.status: assisted factual review recorded; does not satisfy an independent blind first-listener review.
